course_summary:
ISEN 617 | Quantitative Models for Supply Chain Coordination | Spring 2026
Instructor: Joseph Geunes | geunes@tamu.edu
Meets: Online
Grading: Homework Assignments [20%], Quiz 1 [20%], Quiz 2 [20%], Quiz 3 [20%], Quiz 4 [20%] — A: 90-100%, B: 80-89%, C: 70-79%, D: 60-69%, F: <60%
Topics: The Traveling Salesman Problem, The Vehicle Routing Problem, The Bullwhip Effect, Economic Order Quantity, Power-of-Two Policies, Economic Production Quantity, Guaranteed Service Models, Multistage EOQ Type Models, Series Systems with Stochastic Demand, Periodic Review with Zero Fixed Costs, Periodic Review with Nonzero Fixed Costs, Continuous Review, Dynamic, Deterministic Demand, channel coordination models, vendor-managed inventory models, Deterministic Inventory Models, Stochastic Inventory Models, Multiechelon Inventory Models, Integrated Supply Chain Models, Demand Modeling, Forecasting: Classical Methods, Forecast Accuracy, Supply Chain Contracts, Facility Location Models, Pooling, Flexibility, Quantity Discounts, Backorders, Supply Uncertainty, inventory costs, transportation costs, multistage systems, operations tradeoffs, conflicting incentives, coordinate operations, model operations processes, supply chain management, complexities, models, concepts
Tools: ProQuest Ebook Central
